subject: Re: Saturnix Renewal — pricing and term alignment
messages:
From: Helen Cho <procurement@saturnix.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@saturnix.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Saturnix Renewal — pricing and term alignment

Markus —

Thanks for the quick intro last month. Saturnix’s current term with Redwood ends in mid-June (45 days out) and procurement asked I reach out to fast-track pricing and contract alignment so we don’t disrupt our Q3 deployments. We have three items that need to be resolved:

1) Price hold window — procurement would like a short-term price hold while we complete an internal approval (targeting 90 days).
2) Commit levels — we’re forecasting a 35% increase in gen tokens (primarily embeddings + chat) with a phased ramp; we want options to convert part of our retainer into a higher committed tier.
3) Bridge credits / invoice timing — Saturnix is open to a bridge credit to smooth the first invoice if commit changes land mid-term.

I attached a renewal summary (Saturnix_Renewal_Summary.xlsx) with our forecast and procurement timelines. Our preferred cadence: a short written offer (pricing + credit structure) this week, and a mutual action plan (MAP) so legal can prep an amendment. Can Redwood do a short-term price hold and a credit structure tied to a commit increase? If so, what cadence/conditions do you need?

Timeline: Procurement is aiming to issue a PO by 2027-05-31, legal review the week of 6/7.

Appreciate any options you can share — happy to hop on a quick call.

Best,
Helen Cho
Sr. Procurement Manager
Saturnix

Attachments: Saturnix_Renewal_Summary.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Cho <procurement@saturnix.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Saturnix Renewal — pricing and term alignment

Hi Helen —

Thanks for the summary and the timeline. We can definitely work with a short price-hold window while you finalize the PO, and we have a couple of tactical levers that usually help close these fast:

- Temporary price hold: up to 90 days from amendment execution (we typically use 60–90 days depending on billing timing).
- Bridge credit: one-time credit applied to the first invoice if the commit ramp occurs mid-term (amount scaled to the uplift).
- Commit conversion path: we can propose a stepped commit with a phased true-up so you only commit for the parts of the ramp you confirm.

I ran a quick calc with finance and attached a short options doc (Prelim_Uplift_Options.pdf) with 3 scenarios (conservative, staged, and aggressive uplift) showing discount tiers and a sample credit. Would you be able to confirm the expected month-over-month ramp % and whether Saturnix prefers a single amendment or a short-term Addendum + PO? That will determine how we structure the credit and invoice proration.

Also: any regulatory/data residency constraints we should pass to legal? We’ll loop in Contracts when you’re ready.

If this works, I’ll prepare a recommended offer for review with finance and CS (cc’d). Can we target sending that by EOD Tuesday 5/11?

Best,
Markus Klein
Principal Sales Director — Enterprise Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Prelim_Uplift_Options.pdf (PDF, 46KB)
From: Helen Cho <procurement@saturnix.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@saturnix.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Saturnix Renewal — pricing and term alignment

Thanks Markus — this is helpful.

Quick answers:
- Ramp profile: month 1: +10%, month 2: +20%, month 3: +35% (stable thereafter) — embedding-heavy for search + customer support.
- We prefer an Addendum to the current SOW that gets signed with the PO; legal prefers minimal changes to the master.
- Data residency: no changes — stays in us-west.

Procurement would like a bridge credit large enough to cover the first invoice proration while we confirm the middle-months of the ramp (expecting the PO to reflect the new baseline). Ideally the offer would show a sample of prorated billing and the credit applied.

If you can include a short MAP indicating milestones (PO, legal sign-off, go-live for ramp), that will speed internal approvals.

Thanks — happy to take the offer and MAP and review with legal on Thursday.

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, contracts@saturnix.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Saturnix — recommended amendment offer and MAP

Helen / Saturnix team —

Appreciate the ramp detail and the PO timing. Below is Redwood’s recommended amendment to fast-track approval while protecting both sides. We’ll hand this to Contracts as an amendment + MAP.

Summary offer (recommended):
- Term: 12 months from amendment signature.
- Discount: 5% off standard list for the contracted committed tier (applies to gen tokens and embeddings).
- Price hold: 90 days from amendment signature for the agreed committed tier; list prices resume after the period unless a new amendment is signed.
- Bridge credit: $50,000 one-time credit applied to the first invoice to cover proration and ramp variance.
- Commit structure: Step-up commit with a 3-month ramp (10% / 20% / 35%) — true-ups monthly; finance will prorate for mid-month transitions.
- Burst pool: optional 15% burst pool available for short-term load (billed at the committed rate, available with 48-hour notice).

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood to send a short MAP (timeline + milestones) and a one-page Amendment draft by EOD today.
2) Saturnix to confirm PO target and legal contact for redlines.
3) Contracts exchange + signature target: week of 2027-05-31.

We believe this structure delivers the price stability you requested while giving Saturnix operational flexibility as usage ramps. If acceptable, I’ll ask David (cc) to confirm accounting/proration details and Marissa to confirm onboarding/ops readiness for the burst pool.

Marissa — quick confirm that CS can support a 3-month stepped ramp and the optional burst pool with a 48-hour activation SLA?

Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>:
> Confirmed — CS can provision the burst pool and monitor KV cache priming during the ramp. We’ll provide a pre-flight checklist and a short runbook for the go-live.

David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>: any note from finance on invoicing cadence/proration mechanics?

Thanks — I’ll circulate the MAP + amendment doc now.

Best,
Markus Klein
Principal Sales Director — Enterprise Renewals
Redwood Inference
